- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Overestimates prices following sharp upward moves in history (overshoot after spikes).
- Tends to overpredict in the first 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, then gradually converges toward true values — suggesting mean reversion bias.
- Underpredicts when true values show strong downward momentum, especially after a recent high.
- Forecast lags behind true values by 1–3 days in most cases, particularly in the first 10 days of the forecast window.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, especially when true values are rising.
- When history shows a clear trend (e.g., rising or falling), model fails to fully capture the direction, often reversing direction too early or too late.
- Model is overly sensitive to recent volatility, leading to overreaction in short-term forecasts.
